paper.title: Utility Fairness in Contextual Dynamic Pricing with Demand Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Fair contextual pricing with incomplete information (demand learning under delta_0-utility fairness)
unmapped: Generalized linear demand E[y|x,p]=f(x^T theta_0 - alpha_0 p) with known link f and unknown (theta_0, alpha_0); action is a pricing policy mapping contexts to prices in [p_lower, p_upper]
Policies must satisfy delta_0-utility fairness: |pi(x)-pi(x')| <= delta_0 |(x-x')^T theta_0| (w.h.p. for all rounds)
Regret measured in expected revenue against the optimal delta_0-UF policy
Learner needs model constants (M_r, sigma_r, sigma_x, diam(X), delta_0) and a likelihood function satisfying Assumption asmp:likelihood
settings.definition_quote: We adopt a generalized linear model ... \mathbb E[y|x,p] = f(x^\top\theta_0-\alpha_0 p), where $f(\cdot)$ is a known ``link'' function. ... A contextual pricing policy $\pi$ satisfies $\delta_0$-utility fairness if for any $x,x'\in\mX$ it holds that $|\pi(x)-\pi(x')|\leq\delta_0|(x-x')^\top\theta_0|$.

settings.name_in_paper: Fair contextual pricing with incomplete information (lower bound)
unmapped: Generalized linear demand with known link (here linear f(u)=u) and unknown (theta_0, alpha_0); action is a pricing policy
Policies must satisfy delta_0-utility fairness with probability >= 0.95
Regret measured in expected revenue against the optimal delta_0-UF policy
settings.definition_quote: for any contextual pricing with demand learning algorithm over $T$ time periods implementing pricing policies $\pi_1(\cdot),\cdots,\pi_T(\cdot)$, if such an algorithm satisfies $\Pr[\pi_1,\cdots,\pi_T\in\mF_{\theta_0,\alpha_0}(\delta_0)] \geq 0.95$

algorithms.name: Contextual pricing with utility fairness constraints and demand learning (Algorithm 1: price experimentation + MLE + UCB over discretized starting prices)

conditions: algorithm implements delta_0-UF policies in all rounds with probability >= 0.95 for every instance
hard instance: d=1, X=[1/4,3/4] uniform, prices in [0, 3 delta_0/4], Bernoulli demand

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Fix arbitrary $\delta_0\in(0,1/2]$ and let $\underline C>0$ be a strictly positive constant potentially depending on $\delta_0$. Let $f(u)\equiv u$ be the purely linear demand model. There exists model set-up ... such that, for any contextual pricing with demand learning algorithm ... if such an algorithm satisfies $\Pr[\pi_1,\cdots,\pi_T\in\mF_{\theta_0,\alpha_0}(\delta_0)] \geq 0.95$ ... then $\sup ... \mathbb E[\sum_{t=1}^T \max_{\pi\in\mF}R(\pi)-R(\pi_t)]\geq \underline C\times T^{2/3}$

results.notes: Proof sets C = delta_0^(2/3)/123. Regret defined through expected revenue of policies, so recorded as pseudo-regret. Algorithm class: algorithms that are fair w.p. >= 0.95.

bound.regime: with probability 1 - O~(T^{-2}), T sufficiently large

conditions: Assumptions 1-5 (boundedness, smooth strongly unimodal revenue, stochastic contexts with bounded utility density, covariance lambda_min >= sigma_x, regular likelihood)
delta_0 <= sigma_u / M_r (optimal fair policy is linear in utility)

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions \ref{asmp:boundedness}-\ref{asmp:likelihood} hold, and $\delta_0\leq\sigma_u/M_r$ ... With probability $1-\tilde O(T^{-2})$, the following hold: (Fairness) All $\pi_1,\cdots,\pi_T$ satisfy $\delta_0$-utility fairness ... (Regret) $\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E_{x\sim P_{\mX}}[r_x(\pi^*(x))-r_x(\pi_t(x))]\leq (6L_f\tilde B\kappa_1 + 4L_f\kappa_2) T^{2/3}$

results.notes: Equivalent to O~(T^{2/3}) since kappa_1 ~ sqrt(ln(dT)), kappa_2 ~ sqrt(ln T). The same event also guarantees fairness of all policies. Regret is in expected revenue over contexts, holding with high probability over the learning randomness.
